fields.v: University of Toronto, Canada (Tian, Tang, Dong); Xiaohongshu Inc., China (Tian, Wang, Xie, G. Wang); Coolwei AI Lab (Yang); University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, USA (Zhu, You); University of California, Berkeley, USA (Li). Mixed academia/industry; Xiaohongshu supplies the codebase and tasks

Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Compares — benchmark SWE-Bench Mobile (50 feature-implementation tasks from a production iOS codebase, PRD + Figma inputs, diff-based pytest suites) and evaluation of 22 agent-model configurations over 4 coding agents, with cost/time, robustness, a 12-variant prompt ablation and an error analysis

No SDD approach. Agents compared: Cursor v2.3 (Agent mode), OpenAI Codex CLI v0.77.0, Anthropic Claude Code CLI v2.1.37, OpenCode v1.1.44; models Claude Opus 4.5, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Claude Haiku (version not stated), GLM 4.6, GLM 4.7, GPT 5, GPT 5.1, GPT 5.2, Gemini 3 Pro. Prompt ablation: 12 prompt variants (e.g. Baseline, Defensive Programming, Chain of Thought, Test Driven, Comprehensive) on Claude Code + GLM 4.6

Per task (benchmark input, not an SDD artefact): Product Requirement Document (PRD; feature goal, user story, acceptance criteria, constraints; avg 450 words), Figma design in 70% of tasks, reference images in 92%, codebase snapshot; output a unified diff patch. Prompt templates: role definition, task description, output format

Not stated as a prescribed flow. Benchmark pipeline: agent receives PRD + Figma + codebase -> navigates the codebase, plans the implementation and generates code -> outputs a Git patch -> patch evaluated against task-specific test suite

None in the runs (autonomous). Human validation only during benchmark construction (PRD review, test design, reference implementation checked against the tests). Authors recommend human review of agent output in practice
N/A (no SDD approach); agents run end to end on PRD-driven feature tasks
Not classifiable; authors do not use SDD terms (PRDs 'requiring agents to parse natural language specifications')
Existing code base: feature implementation (not bug fixing) in a production iOS application

50 tasks, 449 test cases (9.1 per task); codebase approx. 500,000 lines of Swift/Objective-C, approx. 5 GB; avg 4.2 files modified per task; difficulty Easy 15 / Medium 25 / Hard 10 (Easy 1-2 files and <50 LOC, Medium 3-5 files and 50-150 LOC, Hard 6+ files and >150 LOC)

Mobile application (iOS) of a social media platform (XiaoHongShu, over 300 million monthly active users); categories UI Components 18, Data Mgmt 10, Gesture & Interaction 8, Media & Assets 7, Networking 4, Other 3
N/A (autonomous agents, no human participants). Tasks originally implemented by XiaoHongShu engineers; human validation by the authors and XiaoHongShu engineers
API cost per task (USD; OpenCode via OpenRouter billing); average execution time per task (minutes)
Task Success Rate (% of the 50 tasks where all tests pass); Test Pass Rate (% of the 449 test cases passed); missing patch counts as failing all tests
None
None

Success by number of files modified and patch size (with 95% binomial confidence intervals); success by task category and difficulty; stability across runs (mean, standard deviation over repeated runs for 2 configurations: 3 runs for Claude Code + Opus 4.5, number of runs not stated for Codex + Opus 4.5); failure-mode categories (missing feature flags, data models, files, UI components, methods, incomplete multi-file implementation)
fields.why: The text gives 3 runs only for Claude Code + Opus 4.5; for Codex + Opus 4.5 it says 'stable at 4% across runs' without the number of runs (p. 6)

fields.v: Automatic: pytest suites inspect the unified diff text (pattern matching and structural analysis, no compilation or execution) after static checks on the diff; cost from API billing; time measured per task. Semi-manual: failure categories from test failure messages of the best agents; qualitative analysis of 50+ patches

Criterion (task level): task succeeds when all its tests pass; no configuration-level success threshold. Single run per configuration unless noted. Task Success / Test Pass / cost $ per task / time min (Table 5): (a) Cursor + Claude Opus 4.5: 12.0% / 28.1% / 3.50 / 15.0; (b) Cursor + Claude Sonnet 4.5: 12.0 / 26.7 / 2.00 / 14.2; (c) Cursor + GPT-5.2: 8.0 / 27.4 / 1.80 / 20.0; (d) Cursor + Gemini 3 Pro: 6.0 / 23.2 / 1.00 / 12.5; (e) Cursor + GPT-5.1: 2.0 / 19.6 / 1.10 / 14.2; (f) Codex + GLM-4.6: 12.0 / 19.6 / 1.30 / 13.3; (g) Codex + Claude Sonnet 4.5: 10.0 / 28.1 / 2.50 / 12.5; (h) Codex + GPT-5: 10.0 / 21.4 / 1.50 / 10.0; (i) Codex + Claude Opus 4.5: 4.0 / 20.7 / 3.50 / 14.2 (repeated runs: 4% in every run, SD 0; number of runs not stated); (j) Codex + GPT-5.1: 0.0 / 7.1 / 1.00 / 13.3; (k) Claude Code + GLM-4.6: 10.0 / 26.7 / 1.30 / 11.7; (l) Claude Code + Claude Sonnet 4.5: 10.0 / 24.7 / 2.00 / 13.3; (m) Claude Code + Claude Opus 4.5: 8.0 / 21.8 / 4.00 / 15.0 (3 runs: 6, 8, 6%, mean 6.7, SD 1.15); (n) Claude Code + Claude Haiku: 8.0 / 18.3 / 0.50 / 8.3; (o) OpenCode + GLM-4.6: 8.0 / 17.8 / 0.13 / 32.5; (p) OpenCode + GPT-5.1: 6.0 / 7.1 / 0.02 / 2.0; (q) OpenCode + Claude Sonnet 4.5: 4.0 / 14.7 / 3.50 / 11.1; (r) OpenCode + GLM-4.7: 4.0 / 14.3 / 0.49 / 52.1; (s) OpenCode + Gemini 3 Pro: 4.0 / 13.4 / 0.03 / 8.9; (t) OpenCode + GPT-5.2: 4.0 / 12.0 / 0.04 / 10.9; (u) OpenCode + Claude Opus 4.5: 2.0 / 12.0 / 9.33 / 8.2; (v) OpenCode + GPT-5: 2.0 / 12.0 / 0.18 / 9.8. Ablation (Claude Code + GLM-4.6, 12 prompts, Task / Test %): Defensive Programming 10.0 / 26.7; Quality Focused 10.0 / 26.3; Example Driven 10.0 / 23.4; Chain of Thought 10.0 / 21.8; Baseline 10.0 / 19.3; Explicit Instructions 8.0 / 17.8; Figma Emphasis 8.0 / 18.0; Test Driven 6.0 / 22.0; Detailed Role 4.0 / 20.7; Structured Checklist 4.0 / 20.7; Context Rich 4.0 / 22.7; Comprehensive 4.0 / 22.7. For every configuration: quality: no criterion stated by the authors (authors call 12% 'a significant gap' to industrial requirements, without a threshold); cost: no criterion stated by the authors
fields.why: Values match Tables 4 and 5; but '3 runs' for Codex + Opus 4.5 is not in the text (only 'perfectly stable at 4% across runs', p. 6)

fields.v: Project/tasks: 50 SWE-Bench Mobile tasks on one production iOS codebase. Configurations: 22 agent-model pairs over 4 agents (not a full factorial; each agent run with a subset of models); prompt ablation of 12 variants on one configuration. Baseline: none for the agent comparison; Baseline prompt (P1) for the ablation. Held constant: tasks, PRD/Figma inputs, codebase snapshot, test suites, fixed denominators (50 tasks, 449 tests); Figma/vision access via MCP differs by model (official Figma MCP for vision models, GLM Vision MCP for GLM); prompt used in the main runs not stated. Acceptance tests: hidden task-specific pytest suites on the diff text, built from the PRD and the human reference patch. Repetitions: single run, except repeated runs for Claude Code + Opus 4.5 (3 runs) and Codex + Opus 4.5 (number of runs not stated). Human intervention: none described; iteration limits not stated
fields.why: The number of runs (3) is stated only for Claude Code + Opus 4.5 (p. 6)

fields.v: Best Task Success 12% (Cursor + Opus 4.5, Cursor + Sonnet 4.5, Codex + GLM-4.6); best Test Pass 28.1%. Same model differs across agents: Opus 4.5 12% on Cursor vs 2% on OpenCode (6x); Sonnet 4.5 12 vs 4 (3x); GLM-4.6 12 vs 8 (1.5x). Commercial agents above OpenCode (best OpenCode 8% vs 12%). Success falls from 18% (1-2 files) to 2% (7+ files) and from 20% (<50 lines) to 3% (>200 lines); Easy 18.5% vs Hard 5.8%. Cost: Codex + GLM-4.6 12% at $1.30/task vs Cursor + Opus 4.5 12% at $3.50; OpenCode + Opus 4.5 most expensive ($9.33) with 2%. Prompts: Defensive Programming +7.4 points Test Pass over Baseline (19.3 -> 26.7) with equal Task Success (10%); most detailed prompts 4% Task Success. Failures: missing feature flags 54%, missing data models 22%, missing files 11-15%. No significance tests on differences

Distinguished agents and models only within a narrow range (0-12% task success, i.e. 0-6 tasks of 50); Test Pass Rate shows partial progress. Repeatability: repeated runs for two configurations (3 for Claude Code + Opus 4.5, number not stated for Codex + Opus 4.5), small variance (±1 task); other configurations single runs. Limitations stated by the authors: diff-text tests cannot detect runtime, device or OS issues; one codebase and platform; prompt ablation on one configuration only; costs depend on pricing at experiment time; 50 tasks a snapshot
fields.why: '3 runs for two configurations' is not supported for Codex + Opus 4.5 (number of runs not stated, p. 6)

fields.v: Limitations: single production iOS codebase (no Android, Flutter/React Native); text-based diff inspection, no runtime execution (UI rendering, memory, concurrency); prompt ablation on one agent-model configuration; API costs at experiment-time pricing; 50 tasks may not cover all feature types. Gaps/future work: Android (Kotlin) tasks; simulator-based runtime evaluation; more open-source agents (OpenHands, SWE-Agent) and open-weight models; public API for continuous evaluation; better context retrieval and graph-based reasoning for multi-file tasks; grounding of PRDs and use of visual designs

Reporting inconsistencies: abstract (arXiv v1) says simple 'Defensive Programming' prompts 'outperform complex ones by 7.4%', but the 7.4 is percentage points of Test Pass over the Baseline prompt (19.3 -> 26.7), with equal Task Success (p. 6, Table 4); the published KDD abstract (ACM export) rewords this as 'raise the test pass rate by 7.4 points over the baseline'; 'commercial agents consistently outperform' OpenCode (abstract, p. 1, 5, 7), yet OpenCode + GPT-5.1 (6%) beats Cursor + GPT-5.1 (2%) and Codex + GPT-5.1 (0%) (Tables 5-6); Claude Code + Opus 4.5 is 8.0% in Table 5 (p. 12) but 6, 8, 6% over three runs in Fig. 8 (p. 6); discussion cites a '25% failure rate due to requirement misunderstanding' (p. 7) not given in the error analysis (p. 6-7); failure-mode percentages overlap (sum >100%); the text refers to the category breakdown as 'Table 3' (p. 3) but Table 3 is the cost table (p. 6). Codebase size given as approx. 5 GB (Table 1) and approx. 500K LoC (Table 7). Prompt used for the main 22-configuration runs not stated. Data: tasks and codebase proprietary, not released; hosted evaluation and leaderboard at https://swebenchmobile.com, submission guidelines at https://github.com/realtmxi/mobile-bench. No pre-registration. Programming language: Swift/Objective-C (tests in Python/pytest). Figure 4/5 values garbled in the text extraction; values taken from Table 5 and the text. Full text read is arXiv v1; the published version is KDD '26
fields.why: Missing inconsistencies: the 'consistently outperform' claim is contradicted by GPT-5.1 (OpenCode 6% vs Cursor 2%, Codex 0%); the 'Table 3' cross-reference is wrong; and the published version's abstract corrects the 7.4% wording
